knowledge_point.title: Identifying Matrices in Row Echelon Form

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following matrices are in row echelon form?

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

I. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

II. Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -4 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

- The matrix $B$ is not in row echelon form since the leading entry $b_{21}=-8$ is to the left of the leading entry $b_{13}=-9$ (condition II is violated).

$$
B=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & -9 & -4 \\ -8 & 4 & -1 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

- The matrix $C$ is not in row echelon form since the leading entry $c_{22}=2$ is to the left of the leading entry $c_{13}=-9$ (condition II is violated).

$$
C=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & -9 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & 7 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

Therefore, only $A$ is in row echelon form.
